entities.summary:
Ariaeus was a Persian general who fought alongside Cyrus the Younger at the Battle of Cunaxa and later was involved in the assassination of Tissaphernes. Born in the 4th century BCE, Ariaeus rose to prominence under the rule of the Persian Empire, which at the time spanned from modern-day Iran to Egypt. Ariaeus's military campaigns took him across the ancient Near East, leaving a lasting impact on the region's politics and geography.

Ariaeus played a key role in the Persian conquest of the Ionian cities of Asia Minor, which ultimately led to the Ionian Revolt against Persian rule. His actions also contributed to the decline of the Persian Empire, as his involvement in the assassination of Tissaphernes, a high-ranking Persian official, led to a power struggle that weakened the empire.

Despite his significant contributions to the history of the ancient Near East, Ariaeus's legacy is not as well-known as some of his contemporaries. Nevertheless, his military campaigns and political machinations demonstrate the complex and often tumultuous nature of ancient Persian politics.

The Ariaeus family has left an enduring legacy in the region, with many of their descendants going on to play important roles in the history of the Persian Empire and its successor states.
